clue.text: Improvise in As You Like It?

definitions.meaning: to make something up on the spot without preparation
the Latin phrase ad libitum, shortened, means at one's pleasure, as one likes

explanation.surface: An actor makes up lines during a performance of Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortened Latin tag means freely at pleasure, and as a verb it means to speak without a script.

clue.text: Manage area with two different heads of department

parts.note: the head letter of department is D, and the political head of a government department is a minister
a minister is the political head of a government department

explanation.surface: Running a section of an office where two rival bosses are in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The one phrase is read two ways: the first letter of 'department', and the person who heads a ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer affairs is to run or manage them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Likely to hold up change in the Balkans

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
the word Likely is said to hold the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A forecast that prices in south-east Europe will climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' picks KEL out of 'Likely'; 'up' turns it round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The lek is the currency of Albania, a Balkan country, so it is the change people carry there.

clue.text: American waiter's assistant in tall hat carrying round

indicators.note: the hat word carries the round letter inside it

parts.note: a busby is the tall fur hat worn by some British soldiers, such as the guards
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A restaurant helper in a towering hat brings round the drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A BUSBY is the tall bearskin-style hat of British ceremonial soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: In US restaurants a busboy clears tables and helps the waiting staff.

clue.text: Member of press team's arrived — time for fast publicity to be put out

parts.note: came is the past tense of come, to arrive

indicators.note: the publicity letters are put out of the fasting-month word

parts.note: Ramadan is the Muslim month of fasting
an ad, an advertisement, is publicity

explanation.surface: A photographer has turned up just as a quick press release must be issued.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AD from RAMADAN leaves RAMAN. 'Fast' looks like speed; it means going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or television camera operator is part of a news crew covering events.

clue.text: Band in charts rocks with power

indicators.note: rocks means shakes about, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A rock group climbing the charts with a powerful sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' scrambles IN CHARTS into CHINSTRA, and P is added. 'Band' and 'rocks' lead to music, but the band is a strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinstrap is a band passing under the chin to hold a helmet or hat on.

clue.text: Saw maiden, sober, in pair of spectacles

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: the sober letters sit in the pair of round shapes

parts.note: two round lenses look like the letters O O
TT means teetotal, never drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A young woman, not drinking, looks through her glasses at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see, but it is the noun for a saying. A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, as is a motto.

clue.text: Reminder one must pass in Latin

definitions.meaning: something that brings a fact to mind, here an object recalling death
the Latin words translate as remember that you must die, pass away

explanation.surface: A note in a classical language warning that everyone has to die.
explanation.definitionFit: A skull or similar object kept as a reminder of mortality, named from the Latin for remember you must die.

clue.text: Boy is right to keep up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A lad is entitled to stay awake late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep up' looks like a phrase, but 'up' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil is a boy's name, a typical example of a male given name.

clue.text: Work as seamstress maybe not meant to last

definitions.meaning: a seamstress might make a shift, a simple dress
describing a stopgap thing used only for the time being

explanation.surface: Sewing work is only ever temporary.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift arrangement is a temporary stopgap, not a permanent fixture.

clue.text: Some number leads to doctor in two rings

parts.note: n stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

indicators.note: the doctor letters go in the two numerals

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A few people are directed to a physician at two clinics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' is only a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbi are haloes, the bright rings painted round saints' heads.

clue.text: Holds troop formation together for sailor's memorial

parts.note: a nelson is a wrestling hold, so holds gives the plural
soldiers marching in a line one behind another form a column

explanation.surface: Soldiers keep in step for a naval memorial parade.
explanation.walkthrough: The monument to Admiral Nelson stands in Trafalgar Square, London. A nelson is a wrestling grip round the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The London column topped by Admiral Nelson's statue commemorates the naval hero of Trafalgar.

clue.text: Glasses only needed for this daytime course?

definitions.text: Glasses only needed for this daytime course?

parts.words: Glasses only needed for this daytime course?
parts.note: a midday meal where only drinking glasses are needed, because it consists of alcohol rather than food

explanation.surface: Diners at lunch need only their drinking vessels, no cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: A midday session spent drinking alcohol instead of eating, so only glasses are used.

clue.text: Knowing good fortune comes about through deadly craft

parts.note: fly is slang for shrewd, knowing
in can mean by way of, through
a bomb is slang for a lot of money, as in costing a bomb

explanation.surface: Knowing your luck turns through a dangerous voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes about' is only a link here, so the good-fortune pieces follow 'through'. 'craft' means an aircraft, not a skill: the V-1 doodlebug of the Second World War was the classic example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilotless explosive aircraft, like the V-1 of the Second World War, is a lethal flying machine.

clue.text: Markets stock up, quietly sensing openings

indicators.note: the openings of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Traders restock quietly, sensing opportunities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openings' takes the first letters of 'stock up quietly sensing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Suqs, or souks, are open-air marketplaces in Arab countries.

clue.text: Flying corps hope novice makes college

indicators.note: flying shows the letters of corps hope sent all over the place

parts.note: L, for learner, marks a novice

explanation.surface: An air force group hopes a beginner will get into university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' rearranges CORPS HOPE into PREPSCHOO, and L comes last. 'Flying corps' looks like an air force unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Some fee-paying schools are called colleges, and a preparatory school is one such private school.

clue.text: Determine early broadcast aired porn

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Deciding in advance that adult films were shown on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges AIRED PORN.
explanation.definitionFit: To preordain is to decide or fix something beforehand.

clue.text: Student of old writing English column containing chart

indicators.note: the column word contains the chart word

parts.note: a pier is a pillar or column supporting a structure
a graph is a chart of data

explanation.surface: An English monument carries a diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' makes you think of newspaper text, but here it is a supporting pillar, opened up around the chart.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigrapher studies inscriptions, the old writing carved on stone and similar materials.

clue.text: Spiritualist returned in glory, oddly

indicators.note: returned means the letters picked are read backwards
oddly takes the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of in glory

explanation.surface: A medium comes back, strangely bathed in splendour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes IGOY from 'in glory', and 'returned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A yogi is a spiritual teacher of yoga, a mystic or holy man.

clue.text: So friendly with crowds everywhere

parts.note: as and so both mean in that way
warm means friendly and kindly

explanation.surface: Being so friendly when surrounded by people.
explanation.definitionFit: Aswarm means teeming, full of crowds moving about.

clue.text: Here motorist comes by train, plane and ferry journey

parts.note: a plane is a flat level surface
a trip by ferry over water is a crossing

explanation.surface: A traveller lists his car trip, rail, flight and boat ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train, plane and ferry' looks like a list of transport; 'by train' means beside a train. Where road meets rail, the driver comes next to a train.
explanation.definitionFit: At a level crossing a road crosses a railway on the flat, so drivers come close to trains.

clue.text: Sound from cheap pub relating to ear- Books Fi piece?

annotationWithheld.clue: Sound from cheap pub relating to ear- Books Fi piece?

clue.text: Form of office in Washington

parts.note: the shape of the room the US President works in at the White House

explanation.surface: The paperwork used in a government office in the US capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like a document, but it is a shape: the shape that names the President's office.
explanation.definitionFit: The President's office in the White House is named for its egg-like outline.

clue.text: Churchman joining order generates bitterness

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A cleric receives an honour, causing resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: Ven is the abbreviation for Venerable, an archdeacon's title. 'joining' and 'generates' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is spite or bitterness in speech, beyond its sense of poison.

clue.text: Obtain bar for adjusting part of Venetian

indicators.note: the letters of obtain bar are given for rearranging, adjusted into new order

explanation.surface: Getting a metal rod to fix part of a window blind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusting' rearranges OBTAIN BAR. 'Venetian' suggests a blind, but it is a role in Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Brabantio is a Venetian senator, Desdemona's father, a role in Shakespeare's Othello.

clue.text: Old Indian crown cheers leader in Times re Jaipur

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Old Indian crown cheers leader in Times re Jaipur': 'Times re' is OCR garbage with no job (TA + J from Jaipur gives the answer), the scan is unreadable and a search found no clean text
annotationWithheld.clue: Old Indian crown cheers leader in Times re Jaipur

clue.text: Behold one knight led by bird to king

definitions.text: Behold one knight led by bird to king

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, behold
a hen is a bird
GR, for Georgius Rex, stands for a king
I is one in Roman numerals
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Look at a knight guided to the king by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led by' puts one and knight after bird and king. The whole clue also tells the legend: Wagner's swan knight, brought by a swan to help his king.
explanation.definitionFit: In Wagner's opera the hero arrives in a boat drawn by a swan to serve the king, a knight led by a bird.

clue.text: Chief Justice among the masses? A poor placement

indicators.note: the judge letters go among the crowd word

parts.note: the mob is the common people, the masses
CJ is the abbreviation for Chief Justice

explanation.surface: A senior judge mixing with ordinary people in a lowly role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placement' is a job, and a McJob is a dull low-paid one.
explanation.definitionFit: A McJob is a low-paid, low-prospect job, so a poor employment position.
